newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cocaine found in Maradona's manager's apartment.
newsitem.headline: Cocaine found in Maradona's manager's apartment.

text.p: Argentine police on Wednesday launched an intense hunt for soccer star Diego Maradona's manager Guillermo Coppola after police raided his home and found cocaine that they said was intended for sale.
Judge Hernan Bernasconi ordered the arrest of Coppola after more than one pound (500 grams) of cocaine was found hidden in a large flower vase filled with sand.

"In the police raid we found half a kilo(gram) of cocaine and some tablets, which we still can't determine if they're drugs," he told reporters. "The immediate detention of Mr. Coppola was ordered via fax to various police departments."
The judge said the arrest was ordered on grounds of "possession of drugs for commercial purposes."
Bernasconi has ordered several drug raids in recent days, in which the brother-in-law of Maradona, Gabriel Esposito, and former soccer player Alberto Tarantini were arrested.

"It surprised us (to find cocaine), but the procedure is indisputable because the raid was carried out in the presence of witnesses and Mr. Coppola's lawyers," Bernasconi said. He said he had no evidence against Maradona.
"I can't tell you whether others have been detained but we don't rule out the possibility of carrying out more raids," he added.

Separately, police commissioner Emilio Azzaro said Coppola's apartment has been watched since March. "I think Coppola is still in Argentina. It's difficult to hide with a name that famous," he told local radio.
But Interpol was informed of the arrest order, Bernasconi said.
